//! A tiny word-frequency counter.
//!
//! Fixture for the token estimator tests: Rust with generics, traits,
//! lifetimes, error handling, iterators and unit tests.

use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::fmt;
use std::fs::File;
use std::io::{self, BufRead, BufReader};
use std::path::Path;

#[derive(Debug)]
pub enum CountError {
    Io(io::Error),
    Empty,
}

impl fmt::Display for CountError {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        match self {
            CountError::Io(err) => write!(f, "could not read input: {err}"),
            CountError::Empty => write!(f, "the input contained no words"),
        }
    }
}

impl std::error::Error for CountError {}

impl From<io::Error> for CountError {
    fn from(err: io::Error) -> Self {
        CountError::Io(err)
    }
}

/// Counts of each word, plus the total number of words seen.
#[derive(Debug, Default, Clone, PartialEq)]
pub struct WordCounts {
    counts: HashMap<String, usize>,
    total: usize,
}

impl WordCounts {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self::default()
    }

    /// Adds every word of `line`, lower-cased and stripped of punctuation.
    pub fn add_line(&mut self, line: &str) {
        for word in line
            .split(|c: char| !c.is_alphanumeric() && c != '\'')
            .filter(|w| !w.is_empty())
        {
            *self.counts.entry(word.to_lowercase()).or_insert(0) += 1;
            self.total += 1;
        }
    }

    /// Returns the `n` most frequent words, ties broken alphabetically.
    pub fn top(&self, n: usize) -> Vec<(&str, usize)> {
        let mut entries: Vec<(&str, usize)> =
            self.counts.iter().map(|(w, c)| (w.as_str(), *c)).collect();
        entries.sort_by(|a, b| b.1.cmp(&a.1).then_with(|| a.0.cmp(b.0)));
        entries.truncate(n);
        entries
    }

    pub fn total(&self) -> usize {
        self.total
    }

    pub fn distinct(&self) -> usize {
        self.counts.len()
    }
}

pub fn count_reader<R: BufRead>(reader: R) -> Result<WordCounts, CountError> {
    let mut counts = WordCounts::new();
    for line in reader.lines() {
        counts.add_line(&line?);
    }
    if counts.total() == 0 {
        return Err(CountError::Empty);
    }
    Ok(counts)
}

pub fn count_file<P: AsRef<Path>>(path: P) -> Result<WordCounts, CountError> {
    let file = File::open(path)?;
    count_reader(BufReader::new(file))
}

fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    let path = std::env::args().nth(1).unwrap_or_else(|| "input.txt".to_string());
    let counts = count_file(&path)?;
    println!("{} words, {} distinct", counts.total(), counts.distinct());
    for (rank, (word, n)) in counts.top(10).into_iter().enumerate() {
        let share = n as f64 / counts.total() as f64 * 100.0;
        println!("{:>2}. {:<15} {:>6}  {:>5.1}%", rank + 1, word, n, share);
    }
    Ok(())
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use std::io::Cursor;

    #[test]
    fn counts_words_case_insensitively() {
        let input = Cursor::new("The cat saw the other cat.\nIt wasn't the dog's cat!\n");
        let counts = count_reader(input).expect("input is not empty");
        assert_eq!(counts.total(), 11);
        assert_eq!(counts.top(2), vec![("cat", 3), ("the", 3)]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn empty_input_is_an_error() {
        let result = count_reader(Cursor::new("  \n\n ... \n"));
        assert!(matches!(result, Err(CountError::Empty)));
    }
}
